results.summary_before: This analog project implements an instrumentation amplifier for electrocardiogram signal acquisition, using a three-opamp array to extract low differential signals from noisy common-mode environments. The differential gain is digitally selectable via two input bits, providing 0 dB, 26 dB, or 46 dB gain, with a common-mode rejection ratio of 120 dB. Testing requires a balun, vector network analyzer, and power supplies to measure differential and common responses. The design includes a sense circuit to stabilize the analog ground and is intended for biomedical applications.
results.summary: This analog project models a quadratic integrate-and-fire (QIF) spiking neuron, where the output spikes and resets to a known value when the input crosses a threshold voltage. It uses five analog pins for differential input and output signals and is based on a published compact digital implementation of a QIF neuron. Testing involves applying an 8-bit digital signal and observing whether the output spikes when the voltage crosses the threshold. External hardware listed is an ADLAM2000.
